sonnet.problem: The text says Jehoahaz became king 'In the twenty-third year of the reign of Joash'. The card says Joash 'has been king for twenty-three years', which changes the time the text gives. 'the king before him' is also unclear about whom 'him' means.
sonnet.rule: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

sonnet.problem: The question says the king 'stands beside' Elisha. The text only says Jehoash 'came down to him and wept over him', so this adds a setting. It also clashes with the wrong answer 'sits beside Elisha in silence'.
sonnet.rule: No added settings. No setting the text doesn't give.

sonnet.problem: The card says Elisha is 'sick in bed'. The text says Elisha 'had fallen sick' and never mentions a bed, so this adds a setting.
sonnet.rule: No added settings. No setting the text doesn't give.

sonnet.problem: The story card right before it (card 10) says he should have struck five or six times and then Aram would have been ended. That gives away the answer to this true or false question, which then re-asks the same fact.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'The cities Hazael took from his father' is ambiguous. 'his father' could mean Hazael's father or Jehoash's father, and the text means Jehoash's father Jehoahaz.
sonnet.rule: Clear English. Every card reads correctly. ... 'He,' 'she' and 'they' always point to someone the baker can tell.
